ucie_advanced_reach_mm.source: UCIe electrical summary: advanced package channel reach <= 2 mm (25-55 um bump pitch, 165-1,317 GB/s/mm)

ucie_standard_reach_mm.source: UCIe electrical summary: standard package reach <= 25 mm (28-224 GB/s/mm)

ucie_latency_ns.source: UCIe PHY latency target (TX+RX) 12-16 UI (~0.75 ns at 16 GT/s); adapter included the spec charges 10 ns per hop

lane_gbps.source: 112G PAM4 SerDes class (OIF CEI-112G; IEEE 802.3ck 100 Gb/s per lane)

lane_net_fraction.source: RS(544,514) and 256b/257b transcoding (IEEE 802.3 100 Gb/s per lane PHYs); technology.json rom_board_serdes

lanes_per_package.source: technology.json links.rom_board_serdes.bytes_s note: 128 lanes for a four-die package scaled by sqrt(2/4) -> 90 for two dies

hop_s.source: committed baseline, light (reduced-interleave) FEC package link: 121 ns channel + 4 CDC + 5 endpoint cycles (worktree-agent-a6155059c72eb0abd configs/hardware/technology.json links.rom_board_serdes.hop_latency_s)

hop_flight_included_m.source: technology.json latency_components_s: the 200/121 ns channel includes ~0.3 m of board flight

pcb_ns_per_m.source: stripline ~170 ps/in = 6.7 ns/m (FR-4 class; low-loss laminates Dk 3.3-3.7 are slightly faster)

twinax_ns_per_m.source: Broadcom SUE spec RM104 (2025-09-26) App. A Fig. 22: twinax 4.6 ns per m (Samtec 30 AWG 4.79; Belden 4.3-5.1) -- sync/power validation (research agent adae6788, branch worktree-agent-adae6788cbf2f3f86, technology.json quotes)

dac_112g_reach_m.source: IEEE P802.3ck objectives: twinax (CR) lengths up to at least 2 m; backplane (KR) insertion loss <= 28 dB at 26.56 GHz; RS(544,514) FEC mandatory for CR1/KR1

dac_800g_cr8.source: IEEE 802.3df 800GBASE-CR8: 8 lanes of 100G PAM4 over passive twinax (OSFP/QSFP-DD 800G DAC), <= 2 m class; a stage link of 14 lanes rides two such cables per package per ring neighbour

aec_112g_reach_m.source: Credo 800G AEC (8 x 100G PAM4): 4.0-7.0 m, typ. 10 W per cable

aec_added_latency_ns.source: Point2 P1B121 AEC retimer 3 ns (analog) vs DSP PAM4 retimers ~20x more (~60 ns); an FEC-terminating retimer adds one more KP4 decode (~100 ns). Not needed in this design.

board_trace_budget_mm.source: OIF CEI-112G: XSR up to 50 mm (6-10 dB, 'Lite FEC'); VSR >= 10 cm host trace + 1 connector (16 dB at 29 GHz, pre-FEC BER <= 1e-6); MR 20 dB at 28 GHz; LR 100 cm over 1-2 connectors (28 dB, FEC to BER 1e-4)

serdes_pj_per_bit.source: 5.6 pJ/b per lane incl. analog and DSP at 112 Gb/s (5 nm, VLSI 2022); 7 nm LR 602 mW per channel excluding DSP (JSSC 2021); conservative production value 6.5 -- sync/power validation (research agent adae6788, branch worktree-agent-adae6788cbf2f3f86, technology.json quotes). Was 5 (assumed).

switch_latency_s.source: Broadcom Tomahawk Ultra (shipping July 2025): 250 ns switch latency at full 51.2 Tb/s; sub-400 ns XPU-to-XPU with SUE including switch transit; headers down to 10 B

switch_tray_w.source: no primary source (validation, adae6788): a 51.2 Tb/s switch ASIC ~500-550 W, a 1-2 RU DAC-port system ~1-1.5 kW assumed

ualink_fec.source: UALink 1.0: 'lower latency via 1-way and 2-way code word interleave'; 640-B flit = one RS(544,514) codeword; cable length < 4 m; request-to-response RTT < 1 us

kp4_fec_latency_ns.source: Credo IEEE 802.3cd contribution: RS(544,514) KP4 ~198 ns, RS(272,257) ~99 ns (50GE); Clause 91 RS-FEC budget 409.6 ns tx+rx at 100G

cable_hop_s.source: ring/stage cable hop: full-strength RS(544,514) KP4, un-interleaved -- UALink 1.0's in-rack mode (640-B flit = one RS(544,514) codeword, cables < 4 m); IEEE 802.3ck mandates RS(544,514) for CR1; an RS(272)-class light FEC is not qualified on CR copper (ETC LL-FEC spec 1.0 Annex A Table 1: pre-FEC BER <= 9.9e-5 random, 8.9e-9 under DFE bursts). Cable flight added on top. -- sync/power validation (research agent adae6788, branch worktree-agent-adae6788cbf2f3f86, technology.json quotes). Was 130 ns.

logic_leak_w_per_die.source: 0.10 W/mm2 of logic: H100 71.8 W idle over 814 mm2, TPUv4i 55 W on < 400 mm2 (7 nm) -- sync/power validation (research agent adae6788, branch worktree-agent-adae6788cbf2f3f86, technology.json quotes). Was 33.5 (N5 analytical); non-layer dies scaled by the same ratio

mac_pj_per_op.source: Keller (FP4 at nominal 0.67 V, 38.7 TOPS/W); Jouppi ISCA 2021 Table 2 x0.7 to N5 -- sync/power validation (research agent adae6788, branch worktree-agent-adae6788cbf2f3f86, technology.json quotes)

cdu_fraction.source: CoolIT CHx2000: 12.24 kW per 2,000 kW of IT -- sync/power validation (research agent adae6788, branch worktree-agent-adae6788cbf2f3f86, technology.json quotes) (facility-side, reported beside the rack input)

fan_fraction.source: fans 'a few percent' of IT; 3% assumed -- sync/power validation (research agent adae6788, branch worktree-agent-adae6788cbf2f3f86, technology.json quotes)

ethernet_hop_s.source: an Ethernet port runs the full RS(544,514) FEC (IEEE 802.3ck/df): the full-KP4 hop, technology.json full_kp4_fec_s

hbm3e_footprint_mm.source: Micron HBM3E cube 11 x 11 mm (product brief, via search summary); 1,024 I/O, > 1.2 TB/s per placement

hbm3e_stack_GB.source: Micron HBM3E 12-high 36 GB; >1.2 TB/s per stack

package_mm.source: two ~815 mm2 dies + 8 HBM3E on a ~3.3-reticle CoWoS-L interposer (TSMC today: '3.3x reticle ... eight HBM stacks'); TSMC's 5.5x-reticle interposer 'requires a substrate measuring 100x100mm', so a 3.3x package is below 100 x 100 mm; 85 x 85 mm drawn. B200 substrate dimensions are not published

orv3_ou_mm.source: Open Rack: OpenU = 48 mm; 21-inch (533 mm) equipment bay; 48 V DC busbar

orv3_usable_ou.source: ORv3 racks are built at 44 OU (e.g. ATEN RC8000); NVL72's MGX rack is 2,236 mm tall

orv3_it_width_mm.source: Open Rack equipment bay 21 in = 533 mm (24 in = 610 mm outside)

orv3_tray_depth_mm.source: ORv3 IT depth ~ 800-1,000 mm; 800 mm used for cable lengths

busbar_v.source: ORv3 48 V class busbar; NVL72 power shelves output nominal 50-51 V DC to the busbar

power_shelf_kw.source: ORv3 HPR power shelf: six 5.5 kW PSUs, 50 V 660 A (33 kW; 27.5 kW N+1). Standard ORv3 shelf: 18 kW (15 kW N+1)

vr_efficiency.source: 48 V -> core: Vicor NBM 95.6% at full load x ~0.91 core stage; arXiv:2309.10141 reports >30% delivery loss in AI accelerators -- sync/power validation (research agent adae6788, branch worktree-agent-adae6788cbf2f3f86, technology.json quotes). Was 0.90.

psu_efficiency.source: 80 PLUS Titanium: 96% at 50% load, 91% at 100% -- sync/power validation (research agent adae6788, branch worktree-agent-adae6788cbf2f3f86, technology.json quotes). Was 0.975.

air_limit_w_per_ou.source: no primary source (validation, adae6788): an engineering assumption; ASHRAE TC9.9 (2021) says 1U/2U servers become difficult to air-cool as socket power moves through 300-400 W

air_rack_limit_kw.source: Uptime Institute: above 20-25 kW per rack, direct liquid cooling and precision air become more economical; mean rack 8.4 kW (2020)

tray_mass_kg.source: 1OU liquid-cooled compute tray with 4 packages, cold plates, manifolds

lanes.cable: stage link per package: 14 lanes forward on 2 x 8-lane 800G-class passive DACs (802.3df CR8 class) to the same-position package of the next module, populated 14 of 16 lanes (7 of 8 per cable) so the stage stays inside the 90-lane budget; each populated lane is a duplex SerDes lane whose reverse half carries credit returns, so credits need no extra lanes; the TP link is 13 board lanes per die pair
lanes.note: per package: TP = each die 2 x 13 lanes to both dies of the partner package (R-U8 flat one-shot); stage = 14 lanes to the next module's same-position package, 14 from the previous; switch = 4 lanes (one 400G-class port); 6 spare (lane sparing / debug)

tiers.length: ~1 mm die edge to die edge
tiers.note: the two dies of a package; carries 1 of 3 one-shot peers
package pair on one stage-module board; the two cross-package peers of every one-shot collective

tiers.tier: T2 in-rack copper (stage hop, token return)
tiers.note: folded ring: every ring neighbour on the same or the adjacent tray

tiers.tier: T3 switched copper (Engram, token id, host)
tiers.reach: passive DAC <= 2 m to a mid-rack switch
tiers.note: Ethernet framing with full KP4 FEC on these ports; one 51.2T-class switch
host NICs; ingest lands in the KV-owning stages' HBM through the switch

T4_kv_ingest.note: GPU-prefilled compressed KV + index keys (890 B per context token, FP4 latent + FP4 index key) into the KV-owning stages' HBM through the switch; window rows are re-derived by SWA bounded replay

power.basis: design point: results/arch/v41_hbm_switched.json (energy, rom_worst_die_w) and results/arch/v41_lanes.json static_w, utilisation agent b07a5745 on the spec's validated per-die terms

energy_j_per_token_b1.note: chip = static + dynamic of the ROM dies; wall = x 1.24 + the off-path switch (utilisation agent); rack_input adds the host and management trays

serdes.note: always-on PAM4 lanes; part of the spec's static_w_per_die

reconciliation.note: 116 x the spec's 303 W provisioned per die + 72 table dies + infrastructure, each at 1.2 x wall

paths.note: switched = port hop (full KP4) + 250 ns switch + port hop + ~2.4 m of cable; the table die's row read is charged 100 ns

conflicts.item: ring cable hop on the validated full-KP4 link
conflicts.finding: every ring hop is a <= 0.80 m passive DAC carrying full RS(544,514) KP4 (validated 209 ns, band 160-300) plus 3.7 ns of flight: worst hop 212.7 ns. No retimer or AEC: 802.3ck CR reaches >= 2 m at 100G/lane (802.3dj at 200G/lane only >= 1.0 m, so a 200G-lane refresh sits near the limit).

the light-FEC (130 ns) ring hop is NOT qualified on CR copper (ETC LL-FEC 1.0 Annex A; 802.3ck mandates RS(544,514) for CR1), so the ring runs full KP4, UALink 1.0's un-interleaved in-rack mode (209 ns). This was risk C2; it is now the baseline and costs 29 hops x 83 ns = 2.40 us per token against the 130 ns assumption (Table R-1 geometry row). The on-module T1 board link keeps the light FEC (OIF CEI-112G-MR channel, raw BER 1e-6).

conflicts.item: the baseline mesh is replaced by the adopted folded ring
conflicts.finding: technology.json keeps a 2-D mesh as the generic baseline and HBM-comparator fabric. The adopted ROM ladder already applies ring_placement_return, so the token return is one cable hop, and its stage hops are cut through. The physical folded ring validates adjacency: a module-to-module hop has 0.37 TB/s (28 lanes), so a 41 KB residual serialises in 111 ns, less than the 137 ns priced at 0.30 TB/s per mesh neighbour. The rack sensitivity charges the actual worst cable flight once per hop; no second ring-return credit is taken.

84 always-on 112G lanes per layer/head package at ~0.73 W each = 61 W per package (31 W per die); table packages 1.46 W; 3.60 kW per rack. The rack power scenarios carry it as static. The utilisation record (results/arch/v41_lanes.json static_w) charges 3599 W of ROM SerDes in a ROM chip static total of 14876 W; batch-1 energy 1.762 J per token at 1M at the chips (the comparator's SerDes is charged on the same basis in results/arch/v41_hbm_switched.json).

conflicts.item: HBM interface power scaled to four stacks
conflicts.finding: arch_budget_v41.json kv_state.stacks_per_die = 4 and capacity 962 users at 1M; HBM interface 11.2 W idle per die (4 x 2.8 W) and 34.2 W at full bandwidth (idle + 0.8 pJ/b active I/O), the latter in the spec's worst-case die. The worst case adds full-bandwidth I/O on top of dynamic energy that already charges the actual HBM bytes at 13.1 pJ/b (which includes the I/O): conservative, overlap <= ~2 W per die.

conflicts.item: embedding rows on the head dies avoid the switched token return
conflicts.finding: embedding quarters occupy head dies [112, 113, 114, 115] beside the matching lm_head quarters. The winner reads the next embedding locally and returns it to S0 over one 213 ns ring hop. The former table-die path would have taken 1458 ns; the new placement moves 1.32 GB of Engram spill onto the table dies and leaves every ROM die within capacity. The modeled path saves 1.25 us per token.

conflicts.item: two-die package link bandwidth (T1 on-module TP link)
conflicts.finding: a two-die package has 90 lanes = 1.19 TB/s per direction (1.687 TB/s is the four-die package's 128). R-L9 split: TP 52 lanes = 13 per die pair (171 GB/s per peer), stage 14 + 14, switch 4, spare 6. A 20 KB one-shot partial crosses a peer link in 120 ns; all-reduces whose payload would outlast a board flight run as a fixed-order reduce-scatter + all-gather (each peer receives n/2), bit-identical on every die. Priced on the lanes (collective bytes on their peer links, hops on the stage lanes): 8622 / 23578 tok/s/user at 1M without / with MTP, against 8386 / 18764 at the first rack split and 8,832 with overlap assumed.

conflicts.item: 'point-to-point only, no switch' vs the Engram gather and host/ingest
conflicts.finding: 72 table dies must receive the token id and return 48 rows to S0 (layer 1) and S9 (layer 14); direct cables would need ~36 ports on the consumers. One 51.2T switch carries it OFF the stage path: layer 1's gather completes 1.87 us after the argmax against the spec's 3.57 us slack (margin 1.70 us); layer 14's slack is ~65 us. No token-path collective or stage hop crosses the switch.

conflicts.item: head + DSpark draft KV: SRAM reserve at the fill, HBM beyond it
conflicts.finding: three 128-token draft windows at 528 B per entry and the 28-user fill require 1.42 MB per head die with four-way striping, or 2.84 MB with double buffering. At the assumed N5 SRAM density (0.021 um2 bitcell, 65% array efficiency), double buffering needs at least 0.73 mm2 per head die before banks and ports. Spec ruling (C10): the head dies carry 4 HBM3E stacks each like the layer dies, so users beyond the fill page their draft windows to HBM and all 29 stage modules stay identical. Floorplan (head_draft_floorplan): 112 compiler macros (ot_sram_1r1w_1024x256, 32 KB, 1R1W, repairable), one 4-macro row per user slot = a 1,024-bit read port and an independent write port; a 1.50 x 1.06 mm block (1.58 mm2) that displaces 8.8 MB of the head die's 69 MB spare ROM; macro fmax 1489 MHz at ss, read registered at the macro (2-cycle latency); 6.9 mW leakage. The floorplan is analytical; a routed head-die floorplan remains.

conflicts.item: collective overlap and whole-system clock must be demonstrated
conflicts.finding: the lane-priced rate assumes collective bytes chase their producers (0.93 us of exposed bytes per token) and a 1.087 GHz clock on every die; neither is shown in RTL or routed silicon. With no overlap the stress bound is 8295 tok/s/user. The demonstration plan (record key demonstration_plan) states the benches, parameters and acceptance for both.

ingest_paths.recommendation: Ethernet-switch path: it reuses budgeted ports and the existing switch, gives 53 GB/s per package against 24.6 for PCIe x8, and replicates in the switch. Both paths are hidden under a ~2.9 s cold 1M GPU prefill when streamed layer by layer (ingest agent).

macro.claim_boundary: abstract views from a calibrated analytical model on measured ASAP7 bitcells and ASAP7 standard-cell FO4; no transistor layout, no SPICE of the macro, not silicon; ASAP7 is a predictive PDK and nothing here is a foundry N7 number

organisation.ports: 1R1W per macro: one 1,024-bit read port (the draft attention's window stream) and one 1,024-bit write port (new window rows from the draft pass and from the KV paging engine)

clock.architecture: no rack-wide synchronous clock: every package runs its own PLL from a local reference on its tray; die-to-die inside a package is source-synchronous UCIe; every board/cable link is plesiochronous (IEEE 802.3 PHYs tolerate +-100 ppm) with an elastic buffer in the endpoint's 4-cycle clock-domain crossing
